historical_quarantine.policy: Old fragment matches, proposed keys, rosters, repaired phrases and answer-specific extraction choices are not active targets or validation criteria.
historical_quarantine.reuse_condition: Only reconsider an old result if an independently specified construction and selection rule reproduces it. Do not choose parameters to recover it.

acceptance_requirements: Record clue basis and parameter choices before running a proposed body extraction.
Define the recovered object type and population; it need not be English prose.
Specify what makes one object the outlier before reading its candidate answer.
Check the claimed construction forward, including reversibility where applicable.
Validate nontrivial predictions or structure beyond a short recognizable word.
Keep exploratory hypotheses distinct from author statements and literal source observations.

hypotheses.name: Exact binary-prefix invariants under arbitrary digit relabelling
hypotheses.basis: Execute the representation-first gate left after R13, without adding a semantic keyword or a letterwise encryption. This is exploratory model testing, not an author-confirmed encoding.
hypotheses.model: Each original glyph maps bijectively to a digit of a whole base26 integer; test digits0..25 and bijective digits1..26. Big-endian minimal bytes only. Fixed-width zero-leading numeral allowed conservatively; separately count canonical zero-free A0 numerals.

prefix_families.gzip: 1f8b08 followed by all32 legal flag bytes; remaining header fields unrestricted
prefix_families.zlib: All CM=8, CINFO0..7, FCHECK-valid two-byte headers; FDICT and FLEVEL unrestricted
prefix_families.bzip2: BZh1..9 followed by either the first-block or empty-stream 48-bit marker
prefix_families.xz: Six-byte stream magic only; flags and checksum unrestricted

hypotheses.method: Count all injective glyph/digit assignments consistent with integer intervals for a prefix at each feasible minimal byte length. Fully included prefix subtrees contribute factorial completions; repeated-glyph and all-different constraints prune boundaries. No alphabet enumeration cap or heuristic cutoff.
hypotheses.gate: A zero count excludes only this raw representation and header family. A positive count is prefix compatibility, not a decoded packet, recovered population, or outlier. A deterministic completion is a compatibility witness only.
hypotheses.controls: Compare exact counts with exhaustive small-alphabet permutations; recover known relabelled compressed-header controls; check fixed mappings, bijective bias, leading-zero conventions and boundary inclusivity.

outcome.independent_certificate: All permitted first-six-digit prefixes contradict equality/injectivity for source VXGFAG, or lie outside the numeral range. Independently checked without the interval counter.
outcome.caution: Zlib header-only witnesses are arbitrary completions, not recovered alphabets or validated packets.

hypotheses.name: Little-endian whole-numeral header congruences under arbitrary digit relabelling
hypotheses.basis: Complete the byte-order distinction explicitly left open by R14; no new semantic key, literary population, or letter-stage cipher.
hypotheses.models: Original order; full/drop final I; arbitrary bijective glyph mapping to0..25 or1..26; minimal little-endian integer bytes. A0 zero-leading numeral permitted as in the broader R14 model. For checksum validation of a SAT witness, separately restore0..7 lost trailing zero bytes, as in the earlier whole-integer models; these do not change a header already inside the minimal bytes.
hypotheses.header_families: Exactly the R14 header catalog: all32 gzip flags, all66 valid zlib headers, all18 bzip2 block/empty prefixes, XZ six-byte magic. One disjunction per family, not a preferred header.
hypotheses.method: SMT bit-vector constraints: AllDifferent digits in0..25; sum of modular positional coefficients plus bias equals an admitted little-endian header residue modulo2**(8*header_bytes). Older terms divisible by the modulus vanish. Enforce minimal byte representation long enough to contain the header.
hypotheses.classification: SAT: verify the complete alphabet and header in independent Python arithmetic, then check this one arbitrary completion for a bounded checksum-valid origin-zero compressed stream consuming all bytes. UNSAT: excludes that header family/model. UNKNOWN or timeout: untested feasibility, never a negative.

validation_limits.preset_dictionary: none supplied; a dictionary-required witness is not accepted as a complete stream

hypotheses.limits: No enumeration of all SAT mappings, no model counting, no inference from a lone header; a failing arbitrary witness does not eliminate other maps. SAT alphabets are compatibility witnesses, not recovered keys.
hypotheses.controls: Exhaust small-alphabet permutations against solver SAT/UNSAT; compare modular coefficients with scalar full numerals; known relabelled compressed members; minimal-byte length, bias, exact source roundtrip and timeout-state handling.

outcome.unknown_reason: All four bzip2 queries reached the solver timeout. Feasibility remains unresolved.
outcome.caution: One arbitrary completion per SAT query, not an exhaustive search of compatible alphabets. No payload or population is established.

hypotheses.name: Whole gzip packet with one stored DEFLATE block
hypotheses.basis: R15 shows header-only feasibility is underdetermined. Test a complete low-complexity gzip construction, including the far-end length and CRC, without choosing a keyword. Stored DEFLATE is a standard wrapper for incompressible binary data, not an author-confirmed layer.
hypotheses.models: Raw original glyph order, full/drop final I, arbitrary bijection to0..25 or1..26, whole integer to minimal little-endian bytes, restore0..7 trailing zero bytes. Same alphabet class as R14/R15; no other cipher or book stage.

gzip_scope.header: Exactly ten bytes: magic1f8b, CM8, FLG0 (no optional fields); MTIME, XFL and OS bytes unrestricted.
gzip_scope.deflate: One final stored block: BFINAL1, BTYPE00, any ignored alignment bits, LEN/NLEN complementary; nonempty payload at most65535bytes.
gzip_scope.trailer: CRC32 of the entire stored payload and ISIZE equal to payload length. Must consume every packet byte.
gzip_scope.size_rule: Packet overhead23bytes. For each feasible minimal-byte length n and restoration z in0..7, payload length L=n+z-23. Require the ISIZE trailer to have exactly z trailing zero bytes. Its remaining bytes constrain the high end of the numeral.

hypotheses.method: Convert the high-end ISIZE interval to an exact disjoint cover of glyph/digit prefix assignments; combine that cover with low120-bit gzip/stored-block constraints in SMT. Enumerate distinct numeral-producing assignments, independently reconstruct each whole packet, check grammar, CRC32, ISIZE and bounded decompression.
hypotheses.classification: A verified full packet is a recovery candidate, not an assigned population/outlier. An empty exact interval cover or solver exhaustion with all CRC failures excludes only this stored-block/FLG0 class in that case. Timeout or candidate cap is incomplete, never an exclusion.
hypotheses.excluded: Other DEFLATE block types, multiple blocks, optional gzip fields, multiple members, larger payloads, other wrappers, other byte order, reversed digits, extra letter ciphers, arbitrary offsets, passwords and book transformations.
hypotheses.controls: Exhaust small-alphabet interval covers; positive hand-built valid gzip/stored controls with independent library decoding under both digit biases; CRC corruption, NLEN corruption and nonfinal-block negatives; timeout/cap classifications; exact input roundtrip and source-overwrite guard.

outcome.scope_note: All drop-final-I cases excluded for the registered single stored-block gzip class. Full body5133byte A0/A1 cases remain unresolved; no actual-source CRC candidate was produced. Positive CRC recovery is demonstrated by synthetic controls only.

hypotheses.name: Independent backend check of unresolved R16 packet constraints

hypotheses.budget_note: This is a separately registered second-backend experiment, not a change to the first experiment or a relabelled timeout. No further budget escalation in this pass.
hypotheses.classification: Only completed exhaustion with all candidates independently CRC-rejected proves an exclusion. A timeout or cap remains incomplete. A verified packet must pass the full parser/decompressor and original-letter roundtrip; population/outlier remain unassigned.
hypotheses.controls: Use the same positive full-packet fixtures and CRC-corrupt/candidate-cap controls through the adapter; verify incremental SMT parsing and model values.

outcome.interpretation: Both independently budgeted cvc5 cases remain UNKNOWN. No extension to R16 exclusions, recovered alphabet, packet, population or outlier.

hypotheses.name: Alphabet-independent fixed-width field capacity certificates
hypotheses.basis: R8 registered the key-only count32/key64/checksum32 field interpretation, motivated by the named-construction BLOOM and given/taken hypothesis, but tested only selected alphabets. R14 showed arbitrary alphabets should be handled exactly. No author attribution to IBLT is implied.
hypotheses.inputs: Original raw body, full and explicit remove-final-I. No passwords, letter transforms, offsets, headers, inserted padding or answer fragments.
hypotheses.prediction: Every field must be a nonnegative bit pattern below2**bits, before signed-count interpretation. With w digits and bias a, its most-significant glyph digit d obeys d <= floor(((2**bits-1)-a*(26**w-1)/25)/26**(w-1)). A bijective alphabet cannot assign more distinct leading glyphs than the number of permitted leading digits.
hypotheses.method: Check dimensions; for each field type enumerate original-source most-significant positions and distinct glyphs. Produce a finite certificate of capacity+1 distinct leading glyphs with source indices when the bound is violated. Test against exhaustive small alphabets, independent per-field arithmetic, and synthetic valid fixed-width containers.
hypotheses.classification: Dimension failure or a replayable leading-capacity certificate is an exact exclusion only for the registered raw fixed-width schema/layout/order/bias. Passing the necessary bound is inconclusive, never table recovery. Byte endianness and signed interpretation do not remove overflow.
hypotheses.population_and_outlier_gate: No population or outlier is assigned from a dimension fit or capacity pass; a recovered IBLT would still need independent checksum/hash/peeling and population interpretation.
hypotheses.budget: Finite source traversal only; no SMT, alphabet enumeration on the actual source, semantic scoring or further gzip budgets.

outcome.scope_note: All arbitrary fixed bijections, even separate per field type, fail this raw schema. Other serializations/transforms and named structures remain open; R16/R17 UNKNOWN unchanged.

hypotheses.name: Native shared-RNG layout clock compatibility
hypotheses.basis: R0 exactly reproduces all indentation with consecutive native random.Random(4300).randrange(8) calls. Test whether commonly used letter-generation calls could be interleaved on that same seeded instance while preserving the observed layout, independently of cipher keys or planted text.
hypotheses.historical_overlap: Historical MT tests allowed fixed one/two-word letter/indent interleavings. This experiment explicitly uses native variable rejection for randrange(26) and randrange(8), plus row-granularity byte packing, and records aliasing. No claim that shared-RNG schedules have never been considered.
hypotheses.granularity: Exactly one letter-generation batch for each original row, with its observed letter count. choices uses k=row length; randbytes uses n=row length; other methods draw once per letter. Seed once, no offset/prefix consumption/reseeding/global RNG.
hypotheses.baseline: Consecutive indent calls only; previously known R0 fit, a regression baseline rather than a new discovery.
hypotheses.prediction: For each schedule, reproduce every leading-space count exactly. A mismatch rejects only that direct shared-state recipe. Cipher substitutions or literal message overwrites after generation cannot repair an indentation mismatch without changing the recipe.
hypotheses.instrumentation: Native RNG calls traced by a subclass that delegates unchanged to Python Random. Count 32-bit words for getrandbits and random(), independently compare final states and draws with plain Random controls.
hypotheses.classification: All exact layout matches would be compatible schedules, not proof of the letter generator or recovered population. Mismatches are deterministic schedule failures, not p-values. Group identical full indentation predictions instead of treating aliases as independent evidence.
hypotheses.excluded: Unknown seeds, arbitrary prefix offsets, extra calls, saved/restored state, reseeding, separate RNGs, changed row lengths, rejection depending on plaintext, conditional injection schedules, or comparison to historical word fragments. No actual-source letter decoding or gzip query.
hypotheses.controls: Direct native Random equivalence, independent full-recipe simulations, variable-size batches, native rejection word counts, alias schedules, synthetic schedule recovery without assumed uniqueness, global-state preservation, source overwrite guard.
hypotheses.population_and_outlier_gate: A matching layout alone cannot recover body objects or select an outlier. No message or population is selected in this experiment.
hypotheses.budget: 15 finite schedules, one known baseline, no search over seeds, offsets or alphabets.

outcome.interpretation: These direct shared-instance native recipes fail. The observed layout does not establish a body RNG seed, state or call schedule. Separate instances/reseeding/other generators or schedules remain open; no object population or outlier is recovered.

hypotheses.name: Indel-robust capacity bound for the registered field encoding
hypotheses.basis: Literal one given / one taken can hypothesize one inserted and one deleted source letter. R18 proved only unchanged raw encoding failure; historical packed-object bounds explicitly did not handle phase-changing indels. Test this representation-repair hypothesis without editing the authoritative source or using a preferred output.
hypotheses.operand_hypothesis: Full original body as source of a hypothetical repaired stream, obtained with m deletions and m insertions. Include arbitrary positions and letters, either edit order, coincident substitution-like edits and removal of terminal I followed by insertion elsewhere. m=1 is the registered clue test, not author-confirmed.
hypotheses.target: Exactly the R18 fixed-width count7/key14/checksum7 schema, 312 cells, arbitrary fixed glyph-to-digit bijection A0/A1, both digit directions and layouts. Use key64 overflow only as a necessary condition, not as a decoded IBLT.
hypotheses.method: For each stride and key-leading capacity (A0=8,A1=7), find the maximum run R of consecutive stride-spaced original symbols containing at most capacity distinct glyphs, over every source residue and start. With m insertions and m deletions, at least312-m target key leaders originate in at most2m+1 constant-shift source runs, so312-m <=(2m+1)*R is necessary. If violated, all such repairs fail under every fixed alphabet. Derive the integer lower bound on m, not a sufficient repair.
hypotheses.controls: Exhaustive short-string run maxima, independent brute-force upper-bound replay, exhaustive single-indel-pair targets over a small alphabet, real-schema synthetic valid in-range fields corrupted by paired indels and verified forward, separate bias/capacity checks, certificate tampering, dimension preservation and source-overwrite guard.
hypotheses.classification: A violated inequality is an exact exclusion only for paired-indel repair into this field encoding. A nonviolated inequality is inconclusive, not a recovered table, alphabet or outlier. No insertion/deletion is actually applied to the original file.
hypotheses.excluded: Other field schemas, arbitrary per-cell alphabets, transpositions, additional letter ciphers, unbalanced length changes or interpreting given/taken as operations on decoded objects. No RNG/solver budget escalation.
hypotheses.historical_overlap: Uses the existing capacity principle, now bounding phase-changing paired insertions/deletions rather than only fixed-frame replacements. This is not the first capacity test.
hypotheses.source_refresh: Live gist unchanged: one revision, zero comments,11129bytes, SHA25604eddf97e8ebbc9ce2565269508d63c99b60efc7cacf3f2c020f14215dc67e7e. Refresh is provenance, not a new clue.
hypotheses.budget: Four finite source profiles; no actual-source alphabet permutation, edit-pair enumeration, word search or solver query.
hypotheses.population_and_outlier_gate: No population or answer is selected. Even a feasible encoding repair would require complete hash/checksum/peeling/forward validation and independent interpretation.

outcome.interpretation: Necessary lower bounds, not constructive repairs or IBLT decoding; other representations and decoded-object interpretations remain open.

hypotheses.name: Fixed I-zero strip counts predicted solely from formatting geometry
hypotheses.basis: The user elected to retain final I as a provisional zero and compare individual per-row ranges. R0 reproduces 60-letter rows grouped in fives and indentation, while the archived I-zero analysis reports eight tied patterns. Check whether the counting rule can distinguish row letter contents at all.
hypotheses.model: One original row per strip; zero fixed at the printed final I physical column; counterclockwise; count letters strictly on each side and separately on the guide. For zero-based letter index j in a line grouped in fives with indent d, predicted column is d+j+floor(j/5). Test every actual row without changing it and compare all actual letter positions to formula, not just ranges.

No ciphertext solving, new guide, selected word, statistical scoring or outlier search.

This explains ties and short-row behavior but does not rule out content-aware models, independent vertical guides, encoded intentional edits or downstream object-level outliers.

outcome.interpretation: The fixed-guide letter-count-only range is determined by layout alone and cannot discriminate letter content. Content-aware visual extraction and downstream object-level outliers remain open.

hypotheses.name: Common-substitution mirror pairs around the provisional I-zero guide

Certificate does not recover a population or answer.

hypotheses.name: Any contiguous Ulysses plaintext under arbitrary fixed substitution and transposition
hypotheses.basis: The literal BLOOM acrostic and verified layout-seed 4300 support (but do not confirm) the Joyce/Ulysses Gutenberg 4300 association. hypotheses.name: Whole-training Ulysses running-key offset scan with held-out English test
hypotheses.basis: BLOOM and formatting seed 4300 support an unconfirmed Ulysses link. hypotheses.name: Exact upper-bound replay of all Ulysses running-key training scores
hypotheses.basis: R25 FFT ranked every full-body-eligible C-K book offset by the first 6000 letters, but floating-point ranking is not a formal exclusion. Independently compute a conservative integer upper bound on the training score at every eligible offset. This is a verification and strengthening of the same model, not a new cipher grid or a solver-budget rerun.
hypotheses.model: Same pinned whole Ulysses ASCII normalization, full 8736-letter ciphertext including I, same A0 P=C-K, first6000 training letters, and every offset with room for the entire body. Same fixed English monogram profile and uniform baseline as R25.
hypotheses.method: For each decoded glyph, choose an integer weight w such that w/1000 is a verified strict upper bound on its natural-log likelihood ratio. A native integer worker scans every eligible offset exactly, sums 6000 integer weights and finds the largest upper-bound sum. Verify the 26 inequalities independently using high-precision Decimal exp and a safety margin. If maximum upper bound is below zero, no offset has positive training LLR; in particular none reaches R25’s +0.10 held-out threshold on the training prefix. This is a screen for whole-body English marginal profile, not a necessary property of every English text and not proof no plaintext or short message exists.
hypotheses.controls: Tiny exhaustive worker scores against separate Python scalar oracle for every offset; adversarial ties, fixed full-length boundary and empty/invalid input; synthetic encrypted natural-language-like message matches and passes; selected actual score directly recomputed, hash and overwrite guard; verify upper weights independently.
hypotheses.budget: One deterministic integer exhaustive scan, 1188470 offsets times6000 positions; no new key family, output word search, or SMT/timeout rerun. Record compiler and SHA; protect inputs.
hypotheses.scope: Rules out passing specified positive training score for this direct C-K English-marginal screen only. Does not exclude English with different statistics, short hidden text, intermediate non-prose objects, other operations, cipher alignments, book editions/normalizations, keys, or outlier rules. No proof of solution or book non-use.

outcome.interpretation: Every candidate in the registered C-K book-key family has negative first-6000 English-profile LLR. Not a held-out scan, universal English criterion, short-message exclusion or cipher solution.

hypotheses.name: Held-out fixed-substitution English-frequency mixture across supplied pages
hypotheses.basis: Author says not all layers are encryption and the final answer may be an outlier; full ciphertext need not be English. A real component of English-like plaintext diluted by uniform random background under one fixed substitution might leave a weak marginal signature. Use deterministic batches, no repeated calibration if unpromising.

A negative result does not exclude short or different-language signals, changing alphabets or construction layers. No output words or fragments used.

outcome.interpretation: This page-stable fixed-bijection independent-letter mixture does not generalize. It neither excludes a sparse short payload nor identifies a key or outlier.
